chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And what are the signs and the warners to a people who do not believe?'

He (peace be upon him) said: When the ascension took place for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), Gabriel came to him with the Buraq, so he rode it and came to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and he met those he met from his brothers among the Prophets (peace be upon them). Then he returned and narrated to his companions: 'I came to Bayt al-Maqdis and returned during the night, and Gabriel had come to me with the Buraq and I rode it. The sign of that is that I passed by a caravan of Abu Sufyan being watered at the water of the clan of so-and-so, and they had lost a red camel of theirs, and the people were eager in searching for it.'

So some of them said to others: 'He has come to Syria while riding swiftly, but you have come to Syria and recognized it, so ask him about its markets, its gates, and its merchants.' So they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how is Syria, and how are its markets?'

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when asked about something he did not know, would be distressed until it was shown to him. He said: So while he was in that state, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this Syria has been raised [shown] to you.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned, and there he was with Syria, its gates, its markets, and its merchants. So he said: 'Where are the questioners about Syria?' So they said to him: 'So-and-so and so-and-so.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) answered them in all that they asked him about, yet few among them believed.
And this is the statement of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'And what are the signs and the warners to a people who do not believe?'
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We seek refuge with Allah from not believing in Allah and His Messenger. We believe in Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَبُو سُفْيَانَ: Abu Sufyan (a prominent figure whose caravan served as a sign)
key_terms.النُّذُرُ: The warners (prophets or those who warn of punishment)
key_terms.الْبُرَاق: Al-Buraq (the celestial mount used by the Prophet during the Night Journey)

ai.seo_question: How does the story of the Prophet's Night Journey explain why some people do not believe despite clear signs?
ai.summary: This hadith elucidates the verse 'And what are the signs and the warners to a people who do not believe?' by detailing the Prophet's Night Journey, where he verified his journey by identifying Abu Sufyan's lost camel and miraculously viewing Syria's markets to answer his companions' questions. It highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that despite clear, tangible miracles (Ayat) and prophetic authority, faith remains a matter of divine grace and internal conviction rather than mere external evidence. The Imam concludes by emphasizing the necessity of firm belief in Allah and His Messenger as the ultimate refuge against disbelief.

en.hubeali: H 15002 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al-Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al-Kahily, who has said:
Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Statement of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic: “[10:101] and signs and warners do not avail a people who would not believe”.

Heasws said: ‘When ascension took place with the Messengersaww of Allahazwj, Jibraeel came up to himsaww with Al-Buraaq (the ride). So hesaww rode on it and came to Bayt Al-Maqdas (Jerusalem). So hesaww met the ones whom hesaww met from hissaww brothers from the Prophetsas. Then hesaww returned and narrated it to hissaww companions, ‘Isaww came to Bayt Al-Maqdas, and returned during the night. Jibraeel came to mesaww with Al-Buraaq, so Isaww rode upon it, and the sign of that is that Isaww passed by the camels of Abu Sufyan being watered at the watering hole of the clan of so and so. A red camel of theirs had strayed and the group were looking for it.

So some of them said to the others, ‘But rather he<sup>saww</sup> went to Syria whilst riding at speed whereas you have been to Syria and recognise it. So ask him<sup>saww</sup> about its markets, and its doors, and its businessmen’. So they said, ‘O Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, how is Syria, and how are its markets?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Messenger<sup>saww</sup>, when asked about something that he<sup>saww</sup> did not recognise, he<sup>saww</sup> would not describe it until after seeing it in front of him<sup>saww</sup>. So when they were in the middle of that, Jibraeel came up to him<sup>saww</sup> and said: ‘O Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, this here is Syria which has been raised for you<sup>saww</sup>!’

So the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> turned and visualised Syria, with its doors, and its markets, and its businessmen’. 
So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Where are the questioners about Syria?’ So they said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘It is so and so and so and so (Abu Bakr and Umar)’. So the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> answered them with regards to all of what they asked from him<sup>saww</sup>. Even then they did not believe from among them, except for a few,
and it is the Statement of Allahazwj Blessed and High: “[10:101] and signs and warners do not avail a people who would not believe”.

Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from disbelief in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and in His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>. We<sup>asws</sup> believe in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and in His<sup>azwj</sup> Messenger<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 556. Ahmad Bin Muhammad bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al-Hasan Al-Taymi, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Zurara, from Muhammad Bin Al-Fazeyl, from Abu Hamza who said: ‘I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying:

‘When the believers says to his brother, ‘Uff!’ he comes out from his guardianship. If he says, ‘You are my enemy’, one of the two has blasphemed, because Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic does not Accept the deeds from anyone during the reproach of a Believer, and does not Accept from a Believer any deeds whilst he harbours evil in his heart against a Believer. If the covering is Lifted from the people, so they will see to the Means of what is between Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic and the Believers. Their necks would become submissive to the Believers, and their matters would become easier for them and they would be obedient to them. And if they were to look at the deeds rejected by Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic, they would say, ‘Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic does not Accept the deeds from anybody’. And I (the narrator) heard him (a.s.) say to a man from the Shites: ‘You all are the good ones, and your women are the good ones. Every Believing woman is a beautiful Hourie, and every believing man is a truthful one’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I heard him (a.s.) saying: ‘Our (a.s.) Shites would be the closest of the creatures to the Throne of Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic on the Day of Judgement after us (a.s.). And there is no one from our (a.s.) Shites who stand to Pray except that the number of Angels equal to the ones opposed to him Pray for him in congregation for him until he is free from his Salat (Prayer). And the one from among you who Fasts will be enjoying in the Gardens of the Paradise, and the Angels prepare it for him until he breaks the Fast’. And I (the narrator) heard him (a.s.) saying: ‘You (Shites) are the people Greeted by the Greetings of Allah (azwj), and the people Impacted by the Mercy of Allah (azwj), and the people Guided by the Protection of Allah (azwj), and the people Invited by Allah (azwj) for being obedient to Him (azwj). There is no Accounting for you (Shites), and no fear, and no grief. You are all for the Paradise and the Paradise is for you all. Your names (titles) in our (a.s.) presence are, ‘the righteous’, and ‘the reformers’. And you are the people of the Pleasure of Allah (azwj), Him (azwj) being Pleased with you, and the Angels are your brothers in the good. So if you are striving, they supplicate for you, and if you are in neglect, they strive for you. And you are the best of the created beings. Your houses are gardens for your (living ones), and the graves are the garden for your (deceased). It is for the Paradise that you have been created, and it is in the Paradise that you will be Favoured by, and it is to the Paradise that you are travelling to’.
